My sister lets the power go to her head and while she can generally make my little brother obey her she has a tougher time with me. On Sunday I was gonna go out with my GF for dinner, and my sister stopped me saying that I can't leave. I told her she can boss (little brother's name) around but she can't boss me, and I went out with my GF. I guess my younger brother heard all the commotion and called mom saying we were "fighting" and when I came home and my mom called me she said that I'm grounded and have to dow what my sister says cause she's "in charge". I protested as best as I could but she wasn't having it and grounded me for disobeying my sister who is a pseudo parent while they are away. I just dropped it cause its not worth arguing any point with my mom. AITA here? EDIT:My brother told me afterwards that he was the one that told mom, I forgave him cause I mean I can't be mad at that little turd for too long

This skill can help them prioritize and manage their time more effectively, leading to a greater sense of control and confidence. 4. **Patience and self-awareness**: The demands of childcare can also promote self-awareness and patience, as mothers learn to navigate their own emotions and needs while caring for their children. This can lead to a more mindful and self-compassionate outlook. 5. **Perspective on life's importance**: The experience of motherhood can help mothers appreciate the importance of relationships, family, and community. This can lead to a greater sense of purpose and meaning in life. The constant pressure to be perfect, the weight of responsibility, and the lack of personal time can lead to feelings of burnout, anxiety, and overwhelm. To mitigate these effects, it's crucial for mothers to prioritize self-care, seek support from loved ones, and engage in activities that nourish their minds, bodies, and spirits.
